cells.title: knowledge update: the owner states a new home after an old one, the nightly conflict pass runs, and the current fact is what the store and the recall packet serve
cells.note: measured on Z0 with the live flag ZOE_MEMORY_IMPLICIT_SUPERSEDE=1 (OFF in the code, ON in services/zoe-data/.env): two approved user-stated rows 'User lives in X' / 'User lives in Y' are paired by memory_supersede.conflict_pass (the exclusive home slot) and the older is retired. Without the pass both stay approved and recall serves both

cells.title: knowledge update through a change verb ('moved to'): the new home replaces the old one in what is served
cells.note: the owner's explicit teach lane (voice_fact); 'moved to' is a change cue in memory_supersede.CUES

cells.title: knowledge update when the new fact is written by the per-turn digest (a model writer, anchored on the owner's own words): the current fact must win
cells.note: measured, not assumed: the digest's 'User lives in <new>' contradicts a user-stated row, so the authority wall (#1868) holds it back as a `disputed` candidate (user_stated_derived) and recall keeps serving the OLD home until the owner confirms. Safe against the 2026-10-05 incident, but the update does not land on its own: the decision rule's C1 >= 95% needs either the owner's confirmation in the loop (brain tier) or a rule that lets a verbatim user anchor retire the row. The scripted digest stands in for the model; the dispute question queue needs Postgres and is not run in the lab

cells.title: after an update the old fact is invalidated, not deleted: the row is still in the store as superseded with its invalid_at, and the new row carries its valid_from
history: asked where the owner lived before the move, the recall packet can answer with the old home
cells.lme_map: temporal-reasoning; BEAM knowledge update (the old value)
cells.note: fixed (audit P2.1): a question about how things used to be (memory_temporal.is_history_question) makes MemoryService.search add the facts that were replaced, each labelled 'Before that (...)' so it cannot be read as current; Z0.as_of is the real search(as_of=...). It was FAIL on main: the old row was kept but every read hid `superseded` rows. Controls: `invalidate` (the replaced row is deleted: there is no history to read) and `history` (the history read is off: the row is kept but never served). `supersede` is NOT a control here: with it off both homes stay approved and the old one is served as a CURRENT fact, which is C1's failure, not this cell's

cells.title: a replaced fact served for a history question is LABELLED as history ('Before that'), so it cannot be read as the current one; asked with 'used to'
cells.lme_map: temporal-reasoning (knowledge update: the old value, marked)
cells.note: the same two-home update as C2.history_read, asked another way ('where did I used to live'): the old home must come back AND carry the 'Before that' label (memory_temporal.before_that), never as a bare 'User lives in <old home>' beside the current one. Control `history`: the history read off

probes.query: where did I used to live

cells.title: a dated event: 'my dentist appointment is on <date>' is answered by its date when asked 'when is my dentist appointment', among other household rows
cells.note: the date is the one the owner stated (day first, a month name), kept in the row's text; 40 seeded household turns follow so the row must be FOUND, not just present. The structured event date (valid_from is the capture time) is C4.valid_from_is_event_time

cells.title: validity the owner states ('since <year>') survives into the row and is what answers 'since when have I lived there'

probes.query: since when have I lived in {home}

cells.title: the row's valid_from is the year the owner said ('since <year>'), not the year the sentence was captured
cells.note: fixed (audit P2.1): valid_from is the event time stated in the owner's own words (memory_temporal.parse_validity: 'since 2015' -> 1 January 2015, precision year, basis `stated`); without a phrase it is the capture time, and a model writer never gets an event time. It was FAIL on main: valid_from was always the capture time. Control `event_time` (the parser off: valid_from falls back to the capture year)

events.text: I live in {home}, I have been here since {since_year}
events.speaker: owner_typed

cells.title: stale-fact abstention: a fact the owner retracted ('no longer sees <clinic>') is not served as current when asked
cells.note: the explicit-teach lane: 'User no longer sees X' is an end-cue fact (memory_supersede.CUES), so the nightly pass retires 'User's dentist is X'; the retraction itself stays as the current statement

cells.title: stale-fact abstention when the retraction is written by the per-turn digest: the retracted fact must not be served as current
cells.note: measured: the digest's 'User no longer sees X' contradicts a user-stated row, so the authority wall holds it back as a `disputed` candidate and recall keeps serving the retracted dentist until the owner confirms (same mechanism as C1.update_via_turn_digest)

cells.title: no collateral invalidation: a friend's move retires the friend's old home and nothing else (not the owner's home, not the friend's job)
cells.note: the decision rule's 'C6 0 collateral'. The positive half (the friend's old home IS retired) keeps the cell from passing because the pass did nothing
